title: Your Phone Number Can Be Stolen: Why SMS Codes Are Risky for Crypto
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. In a SIM swap, a scammer tricks a phone carrier into moving your number to their SIM, then receives your text-message codes. Security firms and exchanges such as CertiK, OKX and Coinbase say app-based or hardware-key 2FA is safer than SMS. AI-generated voice. Which 2FA do you use today? Educational only. Not financial advice.

scenes.head: SECURITY WARNING
scenes.hook: YOUR PHONE NUMBER CAN BE STOLEN
scenes.narration: Your phone number can be stolen. Here is why that matters.

scenes.head: THE TRICK
scenes.hook: SCAMMERS MOVE YOUR NUMBER TO THEIR SIM
scenes.narration: In a SIM swap, a scammer tricks your carrier into moving your number to their SIM. Then your text codes go to them.

scenes.head: THE RISK
scenes.hook: TEXT CODES CAN LOG THEM IN AS YOU
scenes.narration: With your number, they can request reset codes for accounts that use text message login, including crypto accounts.

scenes.head: THE FIX
scenes.hook: USE AN AUTHENTICATOR APP OR KEY
scenes.narration: Security experts say an authenticator app or a hardware key is safer than text messages. Many exchanges support both.

scenes.head: TODAY
scenes.narration: Open your account security settings today and switch off text message codes if you can.
